articles.title: Eagles’ Nick Sirianni Faces Questions on Multi-Injury Night for Saquon Barkley
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni provided an injury update on banged up running back Saquon Barkley. The post Eagles’ Nick Sirianni Faces Questio...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles lost a fifth consecutive game Monday night, falling to the Dallas Cowboys 38-21. The 2026 season is quickly becoming a lost season for the Eagles, but it's rather clear running back Saquon Barkley isn't giving up just yet.

Barkley played despite obviously dealing with a leg injury throughout the night. The running back shared with reporters he re-injured his hamstring and tweaked his back on the first play of the game.

Barkley fought through the injuries to provide what production he could. The All-Pro ran for 62 yards and a touchdown.

It was a typical great player delivering what he could to try and provide his struggling team a spark. But with the back drop of the Jalen Hurt blood clot controversy with the Eagles, head coach Nick Sirianni faced questions about what went into the decision to play Barkley and continue to allow him to play after he sustained multiple injuries on the first play.

"Obviously, you saw that he was on a pitch count here today, and there was constant communication to see how he was feeling, to see where he was," said Sirianni. "He came out early in the second half. Again, when you go into something like that, you make sure the player's health is first and foremost. Is he ready to go? Do they feel ready to go? Do the doctors and trainers feel like they are ready to go?

"We felt like that was the case today. But obviously, we wanted to keep a close eye on him. He's tough as heck."

While Barkley ran for 62 yards, he did that with only seven carries. The Eagles also appeared to be careful to almost always give Barkley the ball when he was on the field.

In other words, he wasn't getting any unnecessary snaps. The Eagles didn't bother trying to use him as a decoy.

In addition to the 62 rushing yards, Barkley also had two catches for nine yards.

articles.title: MAX VERSTAPPEN IS STILL THE GOAT — Give Him a Fast Car and Watch F1 Panic Again
articles.summary: Formula 1 fans can argue about the greatest driver of all time until the end of the season. But before anyone writes off Max Verstappen, they might want to l...
articles.body:
Formula 1 fans can argue about the greatest driver of all time until the end of the season. But before anyone writes off Max Verstappen, they might want to look at what he is doing with the machinery underneath him.

The four-time world champion is no longer in contention for the 2026 title. Kimi Antonelli has emerged as the sport's new superstar, and Mercedes has become the team to beat.

But does that mean Verstappen has suddenly forgotten how to drive?

The Car Is the Problem — Not Max's Talent

Verstappen finished third at the United States Grand Prix on Oct. 25, but the result did not tell the whole story.

Red Bull struggled with inconsistent power-unit behavior, tire strategy and a costly pit stop. Verstappen himself said the team had too many issues to fight for the victory.

That is what makes Verstappen so dangerous. Give him a car capable of challenging for wins, and he can turn a race weekend into a nightmare for everyone else.

Red Bull showed exactly that potential just weeks ago. Verstappen won consecutive races in Malaysia and Singapore, reminding the paddock that his speed had not disappeared.

The problem is that his team has struggled to maintain that level of performance.

Remember What This Driver Has Already Done

Verstappen is a four-time world champion. He has delivered dominant seasons, extraordinary qualifying laps and race performances that have left rivals searching for answers.

His 2023 campaign, in particular, was one of the most dominant seasons in Formula 1 history.

That résumé does not disappear because Mercedes has the stronger package in 2026.

Antonelli deserves enormous credit for what he is accomplishing. But comparing drivers requires looking beyond the championship standings. The car, the strategy, the development race and the ability to extract performance from imperfect machinery all matter.

Verstappen has repeatedly demonstrated that he can make the difference when the margins are tight.

Here is the question that should make the rest of the grid uncomfortable.

What happens if Red Bull gives Verstappen a genuinely competitive car again?

The Dutchman has already proved he can dominate when everything comes together. His recent victories also show that he remains capable of beating the best when the opportunity presents itself.

Nobody can guarantee that he would immediately return to winning every weekend. Formula 1 is too competitive for that.

The 2027 development battle could be enormous, and Red Bull has every incentive to make sure its next car gives its star driver a better platform.

If Verstappen gets the machinery he needs, the championship conversation could look very different.

Some fans will always put Lewis Hamilton first. Others will argue for Michael Schumacher, Ayrton Senna or other legends of the sport.

That debate is part of what makes Formula 1 special.

But Verstappen belongs in the conversation, and a difficult season does not erase what he has accomplished. The best drivers are not defined only by how they perform when everything is perfect. They are also judged by how much they can extract when it is not.

Max Verstappen is still one of the most formidable talents on the grid.

Give the man a car that can consistently win, and then tell us he is finished. Until then, the GOAT debate is wide open.

articles.title: ‘We’ve done it!’ Harry Kane’s emotional message for wife Katie Goodland after Ballon d’Or triumph
articles.summary: The Bayern Munich striker became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the prestigious prize
articles.body:
Harry Kane delivered an emotional speech and thanked his wife Katie Goodland after winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday night.

England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane pipped Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the most prestigious individual prize in world football, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the award .

An emotional Kane, 33, spoke for more than 10 minutes on stage after receiving the award at the London Palladium before thanking his long-term partner, Goodland, mother to his four children.

"To my wife, Kate, my best friend," Kane said. "We've been through ups and downs for sure. You're my biggest supporter. I actually felt like you wanted this more than me myself.

"The anxious wait for us to find out, I know it's been horrible for you, here it is - we've done it! You always want the best for me, you sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my dreams, and I know they're your dreams as well, so it wouldn't be possible without you.

"This is a trophy that we celebrate, not me. This is me and you, it's all the family, all our close-knit team, so I just want to say thank you, I love you.

"Can't wait to enjoy this and celebrate tonight for sure. Love you."

Kane also thanked his wider family, including older brother Charlie and his parents, whom were in attendance on Monday night.

"My brother Charlie is here tonight," he said. It didn't seem that long ago we was kicking a ball around the garden, over the park, watching football, talking football, just football mad. I know you tell me you gave me a lot of your footballing abilities, so thank you very much. I appreciate that.

"But to have that love and support from an older brother means the world to me. You travel, you watch, you give up time with your family to support me, so thank you.

"Mum and Dad sitting there as well. What a moment. All those years, the sacrifice you gave me, the support you gave me, the times taking me to training, coming to watch me play all, all around England, all around Germany, no matter where it was, even to this day you're there.

"There was never any pressure from you to become a footballer. It was always about working hard. It was always about improving. It was always about learning and all those traits that you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight. I love you. Thank you very much.

"My kids sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime, especially as we're [the ceremony] a little later than we hoped. So to Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

"I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you. I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much."

articles.title: New-look Scottish rinks eye European curling medals - watch live on BBC
articles.summary: Grant Hardie and Fay Henderson lead their respective Scottish rinks to the European Championships with medals in mind.
articles.body:
A glance at the make-up of the Scotland teams going to this week's European Curling Championship tells a story.

This time last year, the Scottish women took silver and the men bronze. Yet only three of the 10 curlers who comprised those rinks will be involved in Ostrava over the next six days.

So it says something about the strength of curling in Scotland that all of those who travelled to the Czech city on Monday did so with medals in mind.

Fay Henderson and Grant Hardie were among those who competed in Finland a year ago. The former as the alternate - or non-playing member - of the women's team and Hardie as deputy to Bruce Mouat in the men's quartet.

Now, both have ascended to the skip role and lead new teams, both of which earned their place at the event by winning the Scottish Championships earlier this year in the immediate aftermath of the Winter Olympics.

Hardie ended that event on the podium in tears after a second consecutive silver medal. Three months later, he announced he would leave Team Mouat after nine glorious years and become skip of what was Team (Ross) Whyte.

Already ranked in the world's top five, they go into these Euros with one aim in mind. "I think it's quite clear for us we want to go there and win it," Hardie told BBC Sport Scotland. "We'll be going in as a top-ranked team but it's a really strong field."

While no longer a qualifier for the Worlds, the chance to lay down a marker at the beginning of the Olympics cycle is one Hardie and his team are eager to take.

And the feeling is similar for Henderson and her rink. While she stops short of saying gold is the target, a podium place is in her sights.

"I've never actually played a game at the Europeans before but have two medals [silver and bronze], which is a bit of a strange feeling," Henderson says. "But I'd love to complete the set.

"But, really, we want to show the top teams that we're definitely a force to be reckoned with."

articles.title: Steph Curry and Yaxel Lendeborg combine for 55 points to lead Warriors to first win of the season vs. Nuggets, 134-114
articles.summary: Steph Curry and Yaxel Lendeborg combined for 55 points to lead Warriors to their first win of the season on Monday night in Denver.
articles.body:
After dropping three straight games to open the 2026-27 campaign, the Golden State Warriors have secured their long-awaited first win of the season on Monday evening in Denver.

Despite a quiet first half from Steph Curry, the Warriors found themselves leading the Denver Nuggets by four points. Curry uncharacteristically attempted just one shot, a made 3-pointer in 14 minutes of action in the first half. Yet, the second half was a different story.

Curry caught fire as the Warriors ran away from the Nuggets in the second half. In the third and fourth quarter, Curry tallied 21 points on 7-of-7 shooting with a pair of made 3-pointers. Curry finished the game with 24 points on a perfect 8-o-8 shooting from the field.

While it was Curry who helped push the Warriors over the finish line in the second half, it was Yaxel Lendeborg at the center of Golden State's first win of the new season. The rookie continued his impressive start to his debut NBA season with another standout performance. Lendeborg tallied a game-high 31 points on 9-of-19 shooting from the field with 12 boards and six assists in 31 minutes. Lendeborg found success getting to the free throw line, hitting 12 of 13 shots from the line.

Lendeborg has now tallied double-figures in each of his first four games with the Warriors, recording 31 points and 26 points in his last two contests.

Along with Lendeborg and Curry, Golden State's offense was rolling on Monday, with three other players scoring in double-figures against the Nuggets. Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos and Al Horford all notched 11 or more points on Monday.

After getting Tuesday off, the Warriors will end their three-game road swing with a contest against Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball and the Minnesota Timberwolves.

articles.title: Cowboys Week 7 Hero Dealing With Personal Tragedy
articles.summary: It was an emotional return for Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who has dealt with personal tragedy as well as injury. The post Cowboys Week 7...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have had a difficult time figuring out their starting linebacker combinations this season, with the team starting off with DeMarvion Overshown alongside Dee Winters in Week 1, bringing in rookie Jaishawn Barham after Overshown got injured and then, with Overshown returning from his hamstring problem in Week 7, demoting Barham and starting Shemar James for the first time this year in a musical-chairs-style decision.

Getting Overshown back on the field turned out to be a big-time stroke of fortune for Dallas, as he had a memorable interception of a Tanner McKee pass in the fourth quarter to quell any momentum for the Eagles, who were trailing 31-21 at the time. The Cowboys scored a touchdown two possessions later, giving them a dominant 38-21 margin in the game.

Cowboys' DeMarvion Overshown: 'Lost 2 People That Are Close to Him'

Overshown has had his fair share of tough times this season, and throughout his NFL career. Overshown tore his ACL in training camp in 2023, then tore his ACL, MCL and PCL in Week 14 of the 2024 season, an injury that kept him out until last November. Out of the 51 games the Cowboys played since Overshown entered the league as a third-round pick before this year, he played just 19 of them.

Then came the hamstring injury this season, which was supposed to take two or three weeks before Overshown could come back. Instead, it took six weeks. But as he celebrated his return to the field, Overshown did so with a heavy heart as he told Patrik Walker of the Cowboys team website.

From Walker: "DeMarvion Overshown told me the hamstring wasn't the only thing he was forced to deal with the last several weeks. he also lost two people that are very close to him, and the performance he had in his first game back was about honoring them and God. #Cowboys "

Overshown had the interception but also led the team with six tackles and had another pass defended in the game.

articles.title: Hadjar demands change at Red Bull after poor start: 'It's too fragile'
articles.summary: Isack Hadjar has called on Red Bull to redesign the clutch on the RB22 after a poor start at the United States Grand Prix. Hopes for a podium were high after...
articles.body:
Isack Hadjar has called on Red Bull to redesign the clutch on the RB22 after a poor start at the United States Grand Prix.

Hopes for a podium were high after Hadjar qualified third for Sunday's race in Austin. However, a poor getaway left him falling behind the two Ferrari drivers of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton. He went on to finish sixth after Lando Norris also got ahead thanks to a superior strategy.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 after the race, Hadjar said he had done nothing wrong at the launch and blamed the hardware entirely. His comments come after Kimi Antonelli pointed out to Max Verstappen after the race that the Dutchman's Red Bull also "bogged down" at the start.

Hadjar said: "You know, I do everything perfectly in terms of procedure, and then I just have clutch over delivery. These things are just out of my control. It's starting to p*** me off, you know."

The Frenchman went on to add: "The clutch, it needs a redesign because at the moment it's too fragile. It's not coping well with temperatures. Yeah, it's a real struggle."

Hadjar explains Verstappen confusion during US GP

During the United States GP, Hadjar initially resisted Red Bull's instruction to let his teammate Max Verstappen through, fearing it would compromise his own race.

It came at a point after Verstappen had made an early pitstop, with Hadjar yet to make a stop of his own. The delay left Verstappen frustrated as he criticised Red Bull for leaving him stuck in his teammate's dirty air.

Explaining the confusion after the race, Hadjar said: "The problem is, in the end, on my side, I realised it's a one-stop race. And on their side, they're like, 'Oh, it's a one-stop race,' and had already pitted.

"So again, he's coming by like a bullet behind me, and it's a confusing situation for both of us, and then I let him by. But I'm making him lose time because he's in my dirty air. I'm losing time because I have to let him by. And that's because we did not anticipate it was an easy one-stop."

articles.title: ‘Soft as Charmin’ – Fans unimpressed as Pat McAfee complains about Utah students making fun of him
articles.summary: Pat McAfee was not happy with the way the University of Utah mocked him, and went off on them during his show. McAfee was part of the College GameDay crew th...
articles.body:
Pat McAfee was not happy with the way the University of Utah mocked him, and went off on them during his show.

McAfee was part of the College GameDay crew that travelled to the University of Utah to watch the Utes take on the Houston Cougars.

Prior to the event, the University put out a social media post asking fans their thoughts about McAfee, and many of them mocked his antics.

Fans believe Pat McAfee is taking University of Utah students' jokes too seriously

Speaking on his show, Pat McAfee expressed his frustration with the University of Utah and how he was treated by the institution while he was hosting College GameDay over the weekend.

While he appreciated the opportunity to engage with the students, McAfee didn't like the fact that the University's official social media channel shared a video of students mocking him.

McAfee said: "I've really enjoyed this college football season. Did not enjoy University of Utah. Did not enjoy it. You know why I didn't like it mostly? Right before I go out there, okay, right before I go out there, I see the University of Utah's Instagram page, okay?…

"They put out a video, can you do an impression of Pat McAfee? And one kid goes, 'Ah, he's corny.' Another kid calls me creepy.

"Hey, you, you're allowed to do what you— the university puts that out? Like, as I'm about to go out and do an infomercial for the place, and then I'm walking in front of thousands of these people, this is how the university feels about it?

"It's an uncomfortable feeling… I'm getting a lot of shrapnel from a lot of places. The university is putting this out. That is something I just had never experienced really in my entire life. So it kind of set me off a little bit. It made me feel a little bit weird, I would say. Made me feel a little bit weird."

Understandably, some fans did not share sympathy for McAfee, as they felt that he was being overly sensitive about some very lighthearted jabs.

One fan who was in attendance at College GameDay told Pat: "Pat, it was a good College GameDay. To clarify, I didn't say you were corny, and nobody said you were creepy."

Another fan added: "This is such a pathetic response to him reacting emotionally when he should not have. To double down on it is crazy."

A third fan who also attended the University of Utah said: "It really was just that video? That's wild. I thought some other s*** happened for sure. The video was pretty light-hearted. Can't believe Pat is roasting my school over something so soft."

A fourth fan did not hold back on McAfee at all: "A kid said he didn't want to see you shirtless and another called you corny… Where is the deep-rooted hatred? He's soft as Charmin."

A fifth fan added to these comments: "Soft as Charmin. Imagine making millions acting like a frat boy and having a problem with an IG post."

And lastly, one final fan suggested McAfee's success has not made him better equipped to handle criticism: "Bro is more famous than ever and yet is a top-tier loser now."

In response to McAfee's comments, ESPN and the University of Utah both put out statements, with the University apologising for the social media post and deleting it from their social media accounts.

articles.title: Why Troy Aikman isn’t ready to change opinion on Cowboys after beating injured Eagles
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys finally produced the response they desperately needed, securing a win over the Philadelphia Eagles to end their two-game losing streak. Ho...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys finally produced the response they desperately needed, securing a win over the Philadelphia Eagles to end their two-game losing streak. However, despite the convincing result, former Cowboys quarterback Troy Aikman isn't ready to reconsider his concerns about the team.

During the postgame discussion, ESPN's Scott Van Pelt asked Aikman whether Dallas' performance had changed his perception of the Cowboys. However, the Hall of Fame quarterback shared in reply why he wasn't prepared to draw any sweeping conclusions from the divisional win.

"Eh, not really," Aikman said. "Not really. And I don't mean that as a negative. This is a beat-up Philadelphia team. To come in here and win tonight, I mean, let's not get carried away."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Dallas deserves credit for its performance, particularly on offense. The Cowboys finished with 416 total yards, including 204 rushing yards, while protecting the football and avoiding turnovers throughout the game.

Quarterback Dak Prescott played a crucial role in the victory, throwing for 212 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. Running back Javonte Williams also delivered one of his strongest performances, recording 155 rushing yards and a touchdown to help Dallas establish control on the ground.

However, despite the offensive success, the Cowboys' defense still surrendered 21 points to Philadelphia. The Eagles also entered the matchup dealing with significant injury problems, including the absence of starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. Those circumstances help explain why Aikman believes Dallas needs to produce more convincing performances before he changes his overall assessment of the team.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer also understands that a single victory isn't enough to fulfill the team's ultimate ambitions. The Cowboys aren't simply trying to secure individual wins; rather, they are working toward their championship aspirations, which require consistency across the remainder of the season.

articles.title: Why an angry Brian Schottenheimer was short with media following Dallas Cowboys job-saving win
articles.summary: As the Dallas Cowboys ran to the locker room after Monday’s 38-21 victory against the Philadelphia Eagles, the players hooped and trolled Eagles fans in tunn...
articles.body:
As the Dallas Cowboys ran to the locker room after Monday's 38-21 victory against the Philadelphia Eagles, the players hooped and trolled Eagles fans in tunnel with their Fly Eagles Fly dance.

It's understandable for the Cowboys to let off some steam as the win broke a two-game losing streak and kept their hopes of making the playoffs alive at a still disappointing 3-4 mark.

Quarterback Dak Prescott, who tossed three touchdown passes, called it a must-win game and that's how the team approached it.

The players even celebrated in the locker room blasting "Dreams and Nightmares" through the speakers. Dreams and Nightmares" by Philly native Meek Mill is famously the signature Super Bowl-winning anthem of the Eagles.

But when it came to time talk to the press after the game, the normally affable and loquacious coach Brian Schottenheimer was buttoned up and surprisingly short.

His post-game pressers usually last 10-15 minutes. This one last roughly four minutes.

It was the culmination of a trying week for Schottenheimer, who took heat from the media for calling himself a great coach and an elite player caller.

And then there were questions about his job security after going 7-9-1 last season and opening 2-4 in 2026 before Monday's much-needed win.

Owner Jerry Jones said before the game that this was as big a seventh game of the season for the team and the coach that he could remember.

When asked about his attitude, Schottenheimer said he was fine and that nothing was different.

"I'm great. Excited for our guys," Schottenheimer said.

Schottenheimer said he was angry and pissed off early in the week.

Prescott said that's the Schottenheimer he saw on Monday night. He said he is coach was angry and likely perturbed about things that were said about him.

"Definitely hungry, pissed off version of Schottenheimer," Prescott said. "It's not like he's naive. It's not like he hadn't heard some noise about him and whether it's the call in the games or whatever doubt that's been out there, but we've got his back. He knows that. He's a guy that takes a lot of pride in his job, a lot of pride in his team. Everybody handles everything different, so I don't blame him to an extent. We've got his back. More importantly, it's just about us going out there and executing."

Prescott said didn't have an conversations with Schottenheimer about his mindset but you feel it and the team followed his lead with the victory.

"Yeah, it was just evident," Prescott said. "There's actually no conversations about it. I'm not one to talk about that for the most part. The only thing we can do is go control what's in front of us. I think he's very much the same way and I think that's why the hunger was set in. We had a full week of not being able to go back out there and get the win or get the taste out of our mouth from the last couple of weeks, you can say. I was just anxious to get to it, and you can tell we had a great week of preparation, nothing different than we've been doing, but great communication throughout the week and it continued all day today."

"And at the end of day, he's our head coach. We're going to follow him. As I said, we've got his back and we appreciate that."

Here is the full transcript of the Schottenheimer post-game presser:

"We played really well tonight, second half. Had nothing to do with desperation. Our guys should play well."

"I did that to other people. I had headphones on."

On the run game, specifically Cowboys RB Javonte Williams:

"I'm going to start with the offensive end. They were outstanding. Great run plan. But [Cowboys RB] Javonte [Williams], man, the power, the acceleration was there tonight, but great. Then I'm going to talk about [Cowboys RB Tyler Goodson] as well. It was a great change of pace overall. I thought the run game was really good. [The] receivers blocked well. It was a good night."

On the difference in offensive play compared to last year:

"No, it felt good. I thought [Cowboys QB] Dak [Prescott] played awesome. We were good on third downs – 204 yards rushing. It was pretty good. That was good."

"Yeah, again, we've got to be a little bit better against the run. Third down, we tightened up a little bit in the second half. All in all, we held them to 21 points. It gives us a chance."

"Guys were excited. Yeah, it's been a couple weeks coming, but they were excited. We're ready for Arizona. We'll play there in a couple days."

On Cowboys QB Dak Prescott saying the team viewed this game as a must-win:

"No. I thought it was the next championship opportunity. But again, I think it gets us right back into the hunt in the NFC [East Division]."

On Cowboys QB Dak Prescott's performance:

"Just patience and poise in the pocket. It jumped off the film. Anytime you throw three touchdowns like that, the two-point conversion was great. He looked like he was in control out there all night."

On Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown's interception and his insertion back into the defense:

"It was great playing number one. A lot like [LB Dee Winters] last week. The catch was awesome. Put us into a four-minute situation, and it was awesome to see him back out there along with [Cowboys CB] Cobie Durant."

On getting Cowboys WR George Pickens more involved offensively and his success in the game:

"Yeah, solid. Again, spread the ball around. Wanted to run it some more tonight. We did that, but anytime those two guys get open, especially one-on-one, [Cowboys WR] George [Pickens], they're tough."

On the thought process of having Cowboys LB Shemar James starting:

"He's earned it. Great control of what we're doing. Awesome job with the green dot and just proud of his command."

On if he was the only one with the green dot?

"Well, we did rotate some guys through when he came out."

On how important it was to get a win tonight:

"We'll think about this one tonight; really important. Want to play well again next week and beat a good Arizona team."

On whether he has high expectations for Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams:

"Absolutely. He's been great all week. He was fired up about this opponent and did a tremendous job just wreaking havoc inside."

articles.title: Collin Sexton on how he helped sparked the Lakers' comeback on Sunday
articles.summary: Collin Sexton was a major factor in the Lakers' comeback win against the Jazz on Sunday.
articles.body:
Including the preseason, Collin Sexton has played just two games for the Los Angeles Lakers so far, but he has made an impact on the court that has been felt. That impact has gone beyond the numbers that he has put up in both games.

The guard, who signed a two-year, $19 million contract with the Lakers in July, had just five points on 2-of-6 shooting in Friday's 125-117 win against the Los Angeles Clippers . He then scored 13 points on 5-of-11 shooting in 20 minutes on Sunday when the Lakers overcame a big early deficit to topple the Utah Jazz , 132-123 . He had three steals on Friday and no steals on Sunday, but it seems like he came up with more than that, as he did a good job of applying defensive pressure on the perimeter and mucking things up.

Following Sunday's victory, Sexton talked about what he brought to the court at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City and his overall role.

"I would say just come into the game and bring that juice," Sexton said. "Come into the game and try to make an impact on both ends of the court. I feel like tonight, first half I impacted defensively really well and it allowed us to get some stops. Got under their guys and made them put it on the floor. So I think defensively, I was able to impact a lot of it and contribute to the win. So I'm excited."

While Sexton has had a reputation for being a poor defender, he does play with lots of effort and energy on that end of the floor. By playing his man tightly and making his man uncomfortable, teammates can come over and trap that man and force steals, and they can also play the passing lanes tightly and create turnovers that way.

On the offensive end, Sexton can handle the ball, score, hit 3-pointers, create transition opportunities and get others involved. For the first time in a few years, the Lakers appear to have a bench that can come in and change the tenor of a game. Sexton was a major factor in the team turning things around in the second quarter when it outscored Utah 45-24 after getting outscored 47-29 in the first quarter.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo addresses ‘scapegoat’ label amid Heat’s brutal 0-4 start
articles.summary: MIAMI – With the Miami Heat off to their worst start in almost two decades after Monday night’s 113-109 loss to the Dallas Mavericks, it was another disappoi...
articles.body:
MIAMI – With the Miami Heat off to their worst start in almost two decades after Monday night's 113-109 loss to the Dallas Mavericks, it was another disappointing outing for star Bam Adebayo . As Adebayo is off to a slow start with the Heat, he acknowledged the early struggles and how he's been talked about in the sports world.

In the loss to Dallas, Adebayo finished with eight points on making just three out of 10 shot attempts from the field to go along with eight rebounds, three assists, and two steals. This now puts Adebayo at averaging 11.8 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game while shooting 40 percent from the field and 16.7 percent from three-point range.

Heat's Bam Adebayo says outside noise has labeled him as a "scapegoat"

Adebayo has been targeted for his play to start the season, including some former players like Kevin Garnett, who said that the way the 29-year-old is playing isn't "superstar s***." Speaking about his slump, he would address whether the struggles can be linked to the ongoing adjustment process of playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo , leading him to call out the "outside noise" for ousting him as the "scapegoat."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"No, can't overthink basketball, man. For me, it's my shot not going in. I'm not gonna overthink that," Adebayo said to ClutchPoints. "You know, it's funny how the outside noise wants to make me the scapegoat. But when the tables turn, just all that energy…when the energy shifts, just be prepared for that."

" I got expectations for myself , but, obviously, the outside noise got expectations for us," Adebayo continued. "So for me, I know what I'm capable of. I'm not gonna overthink that. Like I said, you know, we're 0-4 right now. I'd rather it be right now than this be midway through the season or in April. Because what if we go on a 10-game winning streak? Then how does the noise change?"

Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo on Bam Adebayo's early struggles

As the Heat continue to get acclimated to Antetokounmpo's play style, the two-time MVP has been impressing with his new team, as he recorded his first triple-double with Miami against the Mavericks. Recording 29 points on 12 of 23 shooting from the field, two of four from deep, to go along with 15 rebounds and 11 assists.

With the vision of the Heat centered around the dynamic duo of Antetokounmpo and Adebayo, the former Milwaukee Buck would say to ClutchPoints that his new star teammate is not alone in the team's rough patch.

"I think it's not just Bam; it's everybody," Antetokounmpo said. "You know, everybody. We try to figure out where we fit in and what we gotta do, kind of try to not step on our toes. I do it myself at times. I find myself just like floating around and trying to like see how to help the team, but at the end of the day, I feel like when I'm at my best, when any player is at his best, is when he's decisive."

"If you're a downhill player, play downhill. If you're a three-point shooter, hunt threes," Antetokounmpo continued. "Then it takes the thought process out of the game. You don't think, you just play, and not just for Bam, for every single person, just play basketball…Slowly, the team will figure it out."

It's a simple fix for head coach Erik Spoelstra , as he believes that Adebayo "just needs to see the ball go in," though they'll put in work to get the star in his comfortable spots. At any rate, it remains to be seen when Adebayo snaps out of his funk, with the next chance coming Wednesday as the Heat look for their first win of the season against the Atlanta Hawks.

articles.title: WNBA Finals: Valkyries beat Dream to reach the brink of their first title
articles.summary: Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton shine for Golden State as Angel Reese’s Atlanta team was stifled by a strong defence.
articles.body:
Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton each scored 13 points to help secure Golden State’s 64-55 victory over Atlanta, putting the Valkyries on the brink of winning the Women’s NBA Finals.

Tiffany Hayes and reserve Cecilia Zandalasini each added 12 points for the Valkyries while Stokes and Burton each pulled down a team-best eight rebounds in Game 5 on Monday.

Golden State seized a 3-2 lead over the Dream in the best-of-seven championship series, which continues on Thursday in Atlanta.

“We’re not done yet. We’ve got one more,” Stokes said. “We need two hoops, 94 feet and each other and that’s all we need.”

The Valkyries, in only their second WNBA campaign, kept Dream star Angel Reese to seven points on 2-of-8 shooting, although she grabbed a game-high 15 rebounds.

Golden State dominated defensively, keeping Atlanta to a season-low in points on 19-of-65 (29 percent) shooting from the floor.

“That has just been our staple all season. We really rely on our defence,” Stokes said.

“They are tough. We have to make sure we’re all doing our part. It’s a team for a reason.”

Stokes had a game-high four blocked shots and has had at least three blocks in every finals game.

Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 20 points while Jordin Canada added 12.

The Valkyries have been a hit with spectators in the home arena of the NBA Golden State Warriors.

“You all are amazing,” Stokes screamed to a cheering crowd moments after the triumph. “We couldn’t do this without you all.”

articles.title: Xabi Alonso Issues Promising Update on ‘Clinical’ Chelsea Attacker
articles.summary: Chelsea are set to play Liverpool in the Carabao Cup in a late October clash. The match has taken on some new importance after the Blues suffered a 2-0 defea...
articles.body:
Chelsea are set to play Liverpool in the Carabao Cup in a late October clash. The match has taken on some new importance after the Blues suffered a 2-0 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge, a crushing blow to morale as they lost to the bitter rivals at home for the first time in many years. Ahead of this cup tie, manager Xabi Alonso was speaking to the media and provided some injury updates to different players including one notable attacker.

Xabi Alonso Issues Injury Update for Attacker Ahead of Liverpool Tie

In speaking about some of his attacking options for the match, the manager seemed very high on one Emmanuel Emegha. The former Strasbourg striker hasn't featured in a professional setting for his new club, but he will be in the squad and is available to play against the Reds.

The coach goes on to state that the youngster has special qualities and that he has a chance to get some minutes in the cup. This is a pretty strong statement backing the striker, who will have big shoes to fill.

With Joao Pedro sidelined and Cole Palmer suspended, the Blues front line will need a lot of help against a very strong Liverpool team. While he is unlikely to start, any minutes for Emegha would give him a chance to build up some fitness and provide cover for the injured Brazilian going forward. As seen against the Lilywhites, playing Morgan Rogers up top left the team without a focal point so getting any natural striker into the fray is a positive.

The return of the Frenchman, once described as a "clinical striker", could be what brings the attack back together in the absence of Pedro. But if not, he and Danny Welbeck can provide cover and offer something a bit more physical in the meantime.

articles.title: Why Minnesota-Indiana was a surprising choice for ESPN's College GameDay
articles.summary: Minnesota will play on another national stage in Week 9 against Indiana.
articles.body:
The Gophers are headed back to the national spotlight, this time as the visiting team for ESPN's College GameDay .

ESPN surprisingly selected Saturday's Minnesota-Indiana matchup as the site of its popular pregame show in Week 9. It'll be just the third time the Gophers have been featured on College GameDay and their first appearance as the road team.

It's another opportunity for Minnesota to make an impression on a national audience in a season that's already delivered several big moments.

College GameDay debuted in 1987 and began traveling to college campuses in 1993, but it took another 26 years for the show to make its first visit to Minnesota.

That came in 2019, when the Gophers hosted rival Wisconsin with a trip to the Big Ten championship game on the line. The atmosphere was electric, though the game itself didn't go Minnesota's way. The Badgers rolled to a 38-17 victory.

The show returned to Minneapolis the following season for Minnesota's Big Ten opener against Michigan, but the experience was drastically different. With the COVID-19 pandemic keeping fans away during the shortened 2020 season, ESPN broadcast the show from inside Minnesota's stadium. The Gophers went on to lose 49-24.

Hosting College GameDay is a special honor for any university, but Saturday will give Minnesota something it hasn't experienced before: a chance to be part of the show on an opponent's campus.

ESPN's decision to head to Bloomington is a bit of a surprise, especially considering the network's lucrative television deal with the SEC and its tendency to feature marquee matchups from that conference.

Indiana is the reigning national champion, but the Hoosiers are also 20.5-point favorites against Minnesota. It's hardly the kind of point spread that screams must-see television.

The game won't even air on an ESPN network. CBS has the broadcast rights, making it just the second College GameDay matchup this season that won't be televised by ESPN or one of its sister networks.

After featuring an SEC team in five of the first six weeks, ESPN is now going three consecutive weeks without showcasing a team from the conference.

And it's not as though the network lacked other appealing options.

Arizona and Texas Tech meet in a ranked Big 12 showdown at 11 a.m. CT on ESPN, while Florida and Georgia renew their rivalry in one of the biggest meetings between the programs in years at 2:30 p.m. CT on ABC.

Ohio State at USC might have been another contender, but the Trojans didn't help their cause by laying an egg at Camp Randall Stadium in Week 8.

For starters, Indiana and Minnesota are both coming off big wins, and the defending national champions are certainly a compelling draw. The selection also gives ESPN another opportunity to push back against the perception that College GameDay disproportionately favors the SEC.

Minnesota has also given the network plenty to work with.

Gophers head coach P.J. Fleck has delivered some memorable moments this season, from his postgame blood ritual after beating Washington to calling the upset of Michigan one of the best days of his life.

Those moments, combined with Minnesota's 5-2 record and 3-1 mark in the Big Ten, have made the Gophers a more intriguing story for a national audience.

Minnesota already got a taste of the national pregame spotlight when FOX brought Big Noon Kickoff to Minneapolis for the Gophers' Week 5 matchup against Michigan.

But College GameDay is the show that helped establish the blueprint for traveling college football pregame productions, and it still carries a different level of fanfare.

Rece Davis hosts the show alongside analysts Desmond Howard, Nick Saban, Pat McAfee and Kirk Herbstreit, with the crew breaking down the biggest storylines in college football before making their picks for the day's top games.

One of the biggest traditions is the celebrity guest picker, and Saturday's show could feature a familiar face.

With College GameDay visiting Indiana for just the third time, it'll be interesting to see whether former Hoosiers head coach Lee Corso is invited to make the picks.

The show will broadcast live from outside Showalter Fountain in the heart of Indiana University's campus. The Pat McAfee Show also typically travels to College GameDay locations, so there's a good chance McAfee's Friday program will originate from Bloomington.

For Minnesota, it's the latest in a growing list of national showcases this season.

The Gophers' Week 2 matchup against Mississippi State landed CBS's 2:30 p.m. CT television slot, the Michigan game brought FOX's Big Noon Kickoff to Minneapolis, and now Saturday's showdown with Indiana will air on CBS while receiving the College GameDay treatment.

The Gophers have had plenty of opportunities to play in front of a national audience this fall. Saturday brings another, and perhaps their biggest stage yet.
